q: Which of the following best describes insurance?
options: A loan given by a bank against future premiums
A contract in which the insurer indemnifies the insured against specified losses in return for a premium
A deposit scheme that guarantees a fixed interest rate
A government subsidy given to households after a disaster
explain: Insurance is a contract of indemnity: the insurer promises compensation for a specified peril and the customer pays a premium for it.

q: The amount a policyholder pays to the insurer for the cover is called the
explain: The premium is the price of the cover. Indemnity and claim relate to what the insurer pays out, not what the customer pays in.

q: Which of the following is NOT a type of general (non-life) insurance?
explain: Insurance is divided into life and non-life. Term life cover protects human life and belongs to life insurance; motor, marine and travel are general insurance types.

q: Life insurance provides a hedge mainly against which kind of uncertain loss?
options: Loss of household income when a life is lost or a person is disabled
Damage to a house from fire
Delay in the arrival of baggage during travel
Theft of goods in transit by road
explain: Life insurance covers contingencies linked to human life such as death, disability and retirement; the other options are general insurance perils.

q: A health insurance policy is a contract between an insurer and an individual or group in which the insurer agrees to
options: Provide a loan at a low rate to the group
Guarantee a fixed return on the premium paid
Provide specified health cover at a particular premium, subject to the policy’s terms and conditions
Pay all medical costs without any conditions
explain: Health insurance is a normal insurance contract: defined cover for a defined premium, subject to the policy’s terms. It is not unconditional.

q: Which type of insurance covers goods in transit by sea, air, rail, road or courier?
explain: Marine cargo insurance covers goods being transported. Marine hull covers the body of ships and boats, while aviation covers aircraft.

q: The hulls of ships and boats can be insured under
explain: Hull insurance protects the vessel itself, whereas cargo insurance protects the goods it carries.

q: Aviation insurance is a specialised policy meant for
options: Passengers who lose baggage on a flight
Goods carried in cargo containers by sea
explain: Aviation insurance insures aircraft such as planes and helicopters. It is one of the specialised property covers within general insurance.

q: Driving a motor vehicle in a public place without insurance is
options: Allowed if the vehicle is new
A civil matter with no penalty
explain: Motor insurance covering third-party liability is compulsory; driving an uninsured vehicle in a public place is punishable under law.

q: Motor insurance protects the owner against damage to the vehicle and also against
options: Third-party liability for injury or damage caused by the vehicle in a public place
Parking fines imposed by traffic police
explain: A motor policy covers own damage and the owner’s legal liability for injury to a third party’s life or property, which is the mandatory part.

q: Which of the following is covered under travel insurance?
options: Fire damage to the traveller’s office
Loss of passport or baggage and unexpected medical expenses during travel
explain: Travel insurance covers accidents, unexpected medical costs, baggage and passport loss, and flight interruptions or delays during travel.

q: LIC of India was formed on
explain: LIC came into being on 1 September 1956 through an Act of Parliament that merged private life insurers. 1972 is the year of general insurance nationalisation.

q: Where is the head office of the Life Insurance Corporation of India?
explain: LIC is headquartered in Mumbai. Hyderabad is the head office of the regulator IRDAI.

q: LIC holds about 49.24 % stake in which bank, making it the only insurer in India to own a bank?
explain: As per the 2024-25 book, LIC holds 49.24 % of IDBI Bank, a unique position among Indian insurers.

q: The LIC IPO of May 2022 was oversubscribed by about how many times?
explain: The IPO, open from 4 to 9 May 2022, was subscribed roughly 2.95 times, with bids of about ₹45,000 crore.

q: Which of the following is the tagline of LIC?
explain: “Yogaksheman Vahamyaham” is LIC’s tagline. “Aapatkale Rakshisyami” is GIC’s; the other two belong to United India and National Insurance.

q: In which year was the general insurance industry in India nationalised and the General Insurance Corporation of India (GIC) incorporated?
explain: General insurance was nationalised in 1972, and GIC was incorporated that year. LIC (life) dates from 1956.

q: At nationalisation of general insurance, how many insurers were grouped and merged into four companies?
explain: 107 insurers were amalgamated into National, New India, Oriental and United India. The 243 figure in the book refers to the life insurers merged into LIC.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four public sector general insurance companies?
options: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd.
explain: The four public general insurers are National, New India, Oriental and United India. ICICI Lombard is a private insurer.

q: GIC was notified as the Indian Reinsurer in which year, ending its supervisory role over its subsidiaries?
explain: GIC became the Indian Reinsurer in November 2000. Ownership of the subsidiaries passed to the Government of India in March 2003.

q: National Insurance Company Ltd. has its head office in
explain: National Insurance is headquartered in Kolkata. Chennai is the base of United India, Mumbai of New India and New Delhi of Oriental.

q: United India Insurance Company Limited has its head office in which city?
explain: UIIC is headquartered in Chennai and was incorporated in 1938.

q: Which of the four public sector general insurers has its head office in New Delhi?
explain: The Oriental Insurance Company, incorporated in 1947, is based in New Delhi.

q: Which general insurer was founded by Sir Dorabji Tata on 23 July 1919?
explain: New India Assurance was founded by Sir Dorabji Tata in 1919, headquartered in Mumbai and nationalised in 1973.

q: “Prithivi, Agni, Jal, Akash, Sab Ki Suraksha Hamare Pass” is the tagline of
explain: The line names the five elements and belongs to Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.

q: Which general insurer was incorporated in 1906 and carries the tagline “Trusted Since 1906”?
explain: National Insurance Company (Kolkata) was incorporated in 1906; its tagline carries that year.

q: At nationalisation, the general insurance operations of LIC’s southern region, along with 12 Indian insurers, 4 cooperative societies and Indian operations of 5 foreign insurers, were merged into
explain: This is the United India Insurance Company’s nationalisation merger; National Insurance merged 21 foreign and 11 Indian companies.

q: Which of the following is the regulator of the insurance industry in India?
explain: IRDAI regulates insurance. SEBI regulates securities markets and PFRDA regulates pensions.

q: Where is the head office of IRDAI located?
explain: IRDAI is headquartered in Hyderabad, with the tagline “Promoting Insurance Protecting Insured”.

q: IRDAI frames regulations for the insurance industry under which section of the Insurance Act, 1938?
explain: IRDAI’s regulation-making power comes from Section 114A of the Insurance Act, 1938. Section 35 deals with amalgamation and transfer of insurance business.

q: Which set of insurers has been declared Domestic Systemically Important Insurers (D-SIIs)?
options: LIC, HDFC Life and ICICI Prudential
GIC Re, New India Assurance and United India
LIC, GIC Re and New India Assurance
explain: IRDAI designated the three state-run insurers LIC, GIC Re and New India Assurance as D-SIIs.

q: The Insurance Ombudsman scheme exists mainly to
options: Settle complaints of individual policyholders outside the courts in a cost-effective and impartial way
Fix the premium rates charged by insurers
Grant licences to new insurance companies
Invest the funds of public sector insurers
explain: The Ombudsman handles grievances of individual policyholders, who can complain personally or through legal heirs, a nominee or an assignee.

q: As per the 2024-25 book, how many insurers operate in India in total (life, general, standalone health and re-insurers)?
explain: There are 68 insurers: 24 life, 27 general, 6 standalone health and 11 re-insurers. Of these, 8 are public and 60 are private.

q: Out of the 68 insurers in India, how many are in the public sector, according to the book?
explain: Eight are public: LIC, the four PSU general insurers, GIC Re, and the two specialised insurers ECGC and AIC.

q: Which two specialised insurers are in the public sector, besides LIC, GIC Re and the four general insurers?
explain: ECGC (export credit) and AIC (agriculture insurance) are the two specialised public sector insurers.

q: Which statement about the number of insurers in India is correct, as per the 2024-25 book?
options: There are 24 general insurers and 27 life insurers
There are 11 standalone health insurers and 6 re-insurers
There are 27 general insurers and 24 life insurers
All 6 standalone health insurers are in the public sector
explain: There are 24 life, 27 general, 6 standalone health and 11 re-insurers; all six standalone health insurers are private.

q: The private sector’s share of the non-life insurance market rose from 13.12 % in FY03 to about what in FY20, per the book?
explain: The book states that private players’ share of the non-life market rose from 13.12 % in FY03 to 55.70 % in FY20.

q: Insurance penetration is best defined as
options: Premiums as a percentage of GDP
Number of agents per lakh population
Claims paid as a percentage of premiums
Share of private insurers in total premiums
explain: Penetration measures premiums as a share of GDP. The book notes it rose from 2.71 % in 2001 to 3.69 % in 2017.

q: Under the tie-up limits discussed in the book, a corporate agent can tie up with how many insurers for each line of business (life, general, health)?
explain: The new limit is nine insurers for a corporate agent and six for an insurance marketing firm (IMF) per line of business.

q: The regulatory sandbox for insurance companies allows testing of innovative products for a maximum of
explain: The sandbox lets insurers test innovative products and technologies in a controlled setting for up to 36 months, with mid-way approvals for faster go-live.

q: Which proposed platform will act as a single source of information to track an existing complaint and file a new one against insurers?
explain: Bima Bharosa is the complaint-tracking platform. Bima Sugam is the proposed marketplace for standardised buying and servicing of policies.

q: Under a “pay as you drive” motor insurance amendment, the premium is lowered mainly on the basis of
options: Kilometres driven, measured by a telematics device
The age of the vehicle’s paint
The number of seats in the car
explain: Pay-as-you-drive links the premium to usage; a free telematics device measures kilometres and reports the car’s health.

q: The “Use & File” procedure allowed by IRDAI mainly helps insurers to
options: Launch and customise products faster and pilot them in smaller groups
explain: Use & File offers more scope for product innovation, quicker go-to-market and small-scale pilots, which improves penetration.

q: Bancassurance means
explain: Bancassurance is selling insurance and banking products through the same channel, usually bank branches.

q: Under the earlier bancassurance guidelines, a bank acting as a corporate agent could sell policies of how many insurers?
options: Three life and three non-life insurers
One life insurer and one non-life insurer
explain: The old norm allowed a bank-agent to tie up with only one life insurer and one non-life insurer. The new norms let banks act as brokers for many insurers.

q: Which statement about RBI’s bancassurance guidelines is correct?
options: Banks may act as corporate agents without seeking prior approval from the RBI
Banks cannot form their own insurance subsidiaries
Banks may sell policies of only one insurer at a time
Banks cannot receive referral fees from insurers
explain: Under the guidelines banks can be corporate agents without prior RBI approval, act as brokers, set up subsidiaries and earn referral fees.

q: Banks that undertake financial services such as insurance business, underwriting and equipment leasing are said to be doing
explain: Services beyond core deposits and lending, such as insurance, underwriting and leasing, are called para-banking.

q: Banks are allowed to form subsidiaries for para-banking activities under which provision?
options: Section 6 of the Pension Fund Act
Section 19(1) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
explain: Section 19(1) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 allows banks to form subsidiaries for specified purposes.

q: Life insurance in its modern form came to India from England in the year
explain: Modern life insurance reached India from England in 1818. 1919 is when New India Assurance was founded.

q: A bank gives a boat loan repayable in monthly instalments over 48 months. Which life insurance would protect the lender if the borrower dies before the loan is repaid?
explain: Decreasing term cover reduces over time just like the outstanding loan balance, so it suits loan protection.

q: Which section of the Insurance Act, 1938 deals with the amalgamation and transfer of insurance business?
explain: Section 35 of the Insurance Act, 1938 covers amalgamation and transfer of insurance business.

q: Postal Life Insurance (PLI) is associated with which Union Ministry?
explain: PLI, in operation since 1884, is run by the Department of Posts under the Ministry of Communications.

q: What was the assured return under the Varishtha Pension Bima Yojana (VPBY) 2017, approved by the Union Cabinet on 24 January 2017?
explain: VPBY, the senior-citizen pension plan approved on 24 January 2017, offered an assured 8 % return at launch.

q: Which of the following is a subsidiary of a bank that offers para-banking services?
explain: SBI Mutual Fund (like SBI Pension Funds Pvt. Ltd and ICICI Ventures) is a bank-owned subsidiary doing para-banking. NABARD, NHB and SEBI are not bank subsidiaries.

q: LIC is governed by which of the following sets of laws and bodies?
options: Insurance Act 1938, LIC Act 1956, LIC Regulations 1959 and IRDAI
RBI Act 1934 and Banking Regulation Act 1949
Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2007 only
explain: LIC is governed by the Insurance Act 1938, the LIC Act 1956, the LIC Regulations 1959 and the IRDAI regulations.
